 Andhra Pradesh After Arnab and Murasu, third cyclone ‘Akvan’ to hit Andhra Pradesh
 Andhra Pradesh is also awaiting a central assessment of the damage caused by Cyclone Murasu and the subsequent financial aid from the BJP led Union government.
 Written by: TNM Staff Published on :  16 Nov 2026, 5:52 am 
 Copied 
 A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm, named Akvan, by the evening of November 16 and further strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by November 17, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said.
 The system is moving north-northwestwards over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal. It is expected to gather strength over the next two days and move towards the Andhra Pradesh coast. This would be the third cyclone to affect Andhra Pradesh in the past few weeks after Cyclones Arnab and Murasu caused extensive damage. 
 The weather system intensified into a deep depression on November 15, when it was located about 640 km east-northeast of Trincomalee in Sri Lanka, 760 km east-southeast of Chennai and 870 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam.
 Andhra Pradesh is also awaiting a central assessment of the damage caused by Cyclone Murasu and the subsequent financial aid from the BJP led Union government. Cyclone Murasu struck the state earlier this month.
 A seven-member central team led by Union Home Ministry Joint Secretary Chittaranjan Das has completed field inspections across Bapatla, Palnadu, Eluru and East Godavari districts. The team examined nearly 60 locations in two groups, assessing damage to crops, roads, drainage systems, houses, irrigation infrastructure and fishing boats.
 During the inspections, officials interacted with farmers at Surappagudem in Bhimadole mandal, examined paddy fields and drainage facilities at Ravulapalem, and assessed damage to the Kommu canal and irrigation infrastructure at Kunakalamarri. Fishing boats at Chirala and houses and horticultural crops at Boppudi were also inspected.
 Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu has urged the team to submit its assessment report within 10 days.
 According to the state government's estimates, Cyclone Murasu caused losses of Rs 2,484.43 crore. Roads and related infrastructure accounted for Rs 888.84 crore, while crop damage across 1,43,617 hectares was estimated at Rs 874.97 crore, affecting 1,86,063 farmers.
 East Godavari reportedly suffered more rainfall-related damage than during Cyclone Arnab. Paddy losses were estimated at 80% in East Godavari and up to 90% in Eluru, with mango and papaya among the worst-hit horticultural crops.
